title: GPX Total Point Counter: Every Point in a File
description: Count every track, route and waypoint point in a GPX file with the GPX Total Point Counter — trkpt, rtept and wpt tallied locally. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a weekend file with two tracks holding 2,100 trackpoints, one 52-point route and 14 waypoints totals 2,166 points — the count this page gives you in one drop.
quick_answer: The GPX Total Point Counter counts every coordinate-bearing point in a GPX file — trackpoints inside track segments, route points inside routes, and standalone waypoints — and reports the total with the breakdown. Drop the file and read the count; everything is parsed locally in your browser.

use_cases.title: Comparing recordings of the same outing

body.t: Two devices, one hike: totals that differ by a few percent are normal; a 10× gap means one file holds a route's handful of points, not a recorded track — the
Point totals size the job before you load a file into GIS or a spreadsheet — 2,000 rows is a glance, 2 million is a database decision.

Track 1: 1,240 trkpt across one segment. Track 2: 860 trkpt. One planned route: 52 rtept. Saved waypoints: 14 wpt. Total = 1,240 + 860 + 52 + 14 = 2,166 points — the breakdown shows tracks dominate, as recorded files always do.

Pausing a recording splits a track into segments, but every segment's points still count. A file with 6 segments and 1,800 points is one outing with five pauses — the total sees the points, not the pauses.

faq: Every <trkpt> in every <trkseg>, every <rtept> in every <rte>, and every top-level <wpt>. The three coordinate-bearing element types of GPX 1.1 — nothing else is a point.
Does a point need elevation or time to count?
No — a point is a point with just its lat/lon attributes. Elevation and timestamps are payload the point may or may not carry.
Can a GPX file have zero points?
Yes — an empty shell with metadata only, or a waypoints-only file can even have zero trackpoints. The counter reports the honest zero with the breakdown.
Routes versus tracks — why separate counts?
Because they mean different things: a route is a plan (sparse), a track is a recording (dense). Totals that mix them mislead; the breakdown keeps them honest.
Vendor extensions can nest extra data, but coordinates inside proprietary extension blobs are not standard GPX points and are not counted as such.
Can I count points per track, not just total?
The breakdown by family is the page's grain; per-track statistics live in the GPX Route Stats family of tools.
Is the count affected by duplicate points?
No — counting is not cleaning. Stationary GPS drift can stack near-identical points; deduplication is a separate, deliberate step.
